newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert birth control pill available.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert birth control pill available.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co said on Thursday that its new class of birth control pills is now available at drug stores.
Warner-Lambert said its Estrostep, low-estrogen birth control pill, is the first new class of oral contraceptives in 10 years.

"Our theory in developing a graduated estrogen oral contraceptive was that i would expose women to relatively low doses of estrogen at the beginning of the cycle, and thus, would be relatively well tolerated," Dr. Leon Speroff, an early researcher on this class of drug, said in a statement.

Higher doses of estrogen in birth control pills led to side effects such as nausea and break-through bleeding, Warner-Lambert said. The side effects are a key reason why women stop using the contraceptive, Warner-Lambert said.
Estrostep uses low, gradually increasing doses of estrogen with 35 milligrams being the highest dose for the last nine days of a woman's menstrual cycle, Warner-Lambert said.
The most common birth control pill uses a steady dose of 35 mg of estrogen for the entire month and early forms of the pill were as high as 150 mg, Warner-Lambert said.
